title: The first words Jesus spoke from the cross were not anger.
paragraphs: The first words Jesus spoke from the cross were not anger.
They were forgiveness.

Not after the pain ended.
Not after the crowd apologized.
While the nails were still in His hands…
Jesus said:
“Father, forgive them.”

The soldiers had just nailed Him to wood.
The crowd mocked Him.
Religious leaders celebrated what they thought was victory.
Yet Jesus prayed for them.
Not against them.
The cross reveals a truth many people struggle to accept:
Forgiveness does not wait for people to deserve it.
Forgiveness flows from a heart that refuses to let hatred win.
If Jesus had chosen revenge, the cross would have become a symbol of judgment.
Instead, it became the greatest symbol of mercy the world has ever seen.
The cross teaches us something deeply challenging:

You can be wounded…
betrayed…
misunderstood…
and still choose forgiveness.
Because forgiveness is not about excusing what happened.
It is about refusing to let pain write the final chapter of your life.
One day the same city that shouted “Crucify Him” would hear the gospel preached in power.
Thousands would repent.
And perhaps it began with a prayer spoken from a cross.
“Father, forgive them.”
The prayer of Jesus echoes through history.
And it still asks us the same question today:
If Christ forgave us at our worst…
Who are we still refusing to forgive?
